solar_array.name: Solar Array
solar_array.summary: Vertical panels that track the low polar Sun. 90 kWh per day in full sunlight.
solar_array.benefit: Free energy while the Sun shines.
solar_array.tradeoff: Produces almost nothing in shadow and gets covered by lunar dust.

science.text: At the lunar poles the Sun stays near the horizon, so arrays are mounted vertically and rotate to follow it. Terrain can shadow them for days.

battery.name: Battery Storage
battery.summary: Lithium-ion pack storing 60 kWh for when the Sun is gone.
battery.benefit: Keeps life support running through shadow periods.
battery.tradeoff: Heavy: about 240 Wh per kg. Stores energy but never produces it.

science.text: Space-rated lithium-ion batteries store roughly 150–250 Wh per kilogram. Energy storage is often the heaviest part of a surface power system.

water_recycler.name: Water Recycler
water_recycler.summary: Recovers 93% of the water the crew uses — from humidity, washing and urine.
water_recycler.tradeoff: Heavy, needs power every day, and can break.

science.text: The ISS Water Recovery System reclaims around 93% of water; with the Brine Processor it reached 98% in 2023.

greenhouse.name: Greenhouse
greenhouse.summary: LED-lit hydroponic racks. After 7 days of growth: 2 kg food and 0.8 kg oxygen per day.
greenhouse.benefit: Food and oxygen made on the Moon.
greenhouse.tradeoff: Hungry for power and water, slow to start, and crops can get sick.

science.text: NASA's Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat have grown lettuce, radishes and peppers on the ISS. Plants turn CO₂ into oxygen, but need lots of light energy.

oxygen_generator.name: Oxygen Generator
oxygen_generator.summary: Splits water into oxygen and hydrogen with electricity (electrolysis). Up to 4 kg O₂ per day; it throttles to keep about 10 days of oxygen in reserve.
oxygen_generator.tradeoff: Uses 1.125 kg of water for every kg of oxygen, and a lot of power.

science.text: Electrolysis: 2 H₂O → 2 H₂ + O₂. By molar mass, 1 kg of oxygen needs 1.125 kg of water. The ISS Oxygen Generation Assembly works this way.

radiation_shelter.name: Radiation Shelter
radiation_shelter.summary: Small room buried under bags of lunar soil (regolith). Blocks ~90% of solar-storm radiation.
radiation_shelter.benefit: Protects the crew during solar storms.
radiation_shelter.tradeoff: The heaviest item you can bring — and useless on a calm day.

science.text: A few tens of g/cm² of regolith or water stop most solar-storm protons. Galactic cosmic rays are far harder to block.

water_crate.name: Water Tank
water_crate.summary: 100 kg of water in a 15 kg tank.

science.text: An astronaut needs about 3.5 kg of water per day for drinking, food and basic hygiene.

oxygen_tank.name: Oxygen Tank
oxygen_tank.summary: 20 kg of compressed oxygen. The high-pressure tank weighs more than the gas.

science.text: Each astronaut breathes about 0.84 kg of oxygen per day.
Space food, including packaging, weighs about 1.8 kg per astronaut per day.

spare_parts.name: Spare Parts Kit
spare_parts.summary: Pumps, valves, seals and circuit boards. One kit fixes one broken system.

science.text: The Moon is 3 days from Earth — you can't order a replacement part. Missions carry spares for the systems most likely to fail.
